now.text: We have 105 distinct questions with recorded speech and the spoken Assistant cue.
The 30B reader gives 13 complete answers out of 20 with full transcripts, but only four with our current notes.
Fix the notes and check longer histories before running speech experiments.
Compare when to start pre-thinking and what work it should do.

definition.text: Doing useful private work before a user asks a question.

items.text: Keep 20 reviewed questions across six meetings, with answer facts and six clips of ordinary discussion.
Preserve the question recordings and keep evaluation speakers separate from earlier voice-tuning speakers.
Collect independent listening ratings before making stronger claims about voice quality and naturalness.
Compare full transcripts, recent speech, transcripts without speaker labels and automatic notes.
Review task owners, changed decisions, missing facts and unreliable earlier reasoning outputs.
The first note system loses useful facts and is not ready for speech tests.

stages.title: 3. Test when and what to think

items.text: Fix task owners, changed decisions and forgotten rules in the notes.
Check that S1 keeps listening and S2 can access older facts as history grows.
Run the original three audio questions through the four system conditions.
Compare waiting for the request with pre-thinking every 30 seconds or after a meaningful change.
Compare summaries, facts with owners and status, and small deductions while keeping update times fixed.
Hide future questions, count all pre-thinking work and measure the first correct useful answer.

stages.title: 4. Add tools and learn when to act

items.text: Add one document lookup with known results and a case where later speech changes the request.
Compare simple rules for listening, pre-thinking, answering, asking, using a tool and cancelling work.
Train an action policy only after the rules and scoring are reliable.
